subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` be an isolated writable workspace, or remain the read-only/no-write profile currently encoded on main and in the latest release?
rationale: Both interpretations have evidence: users need isolated writable scratch space for skills, while merged history and current tests intentionally use read-only behavior as a security posture.

options.title: Approve isolated-writable `none`
options.body: Restore writable mount and fs-bridge semantics for the sandbox workspace only, with explicit tests that `/agent`, real workspace paths, and skill roots remain protected.

options.title: Keep `none` read-only
options.body: Document `none` as a no-write profile and direct writable isolated workflows to an approved alternative such as `rw`, custom binds, or a new mode.

options.title: Add a new explicit mode
options.body: Preserve current `none` semantics and introduce a separately named isolated-writable mode after config and migration review.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated-writable `none`
recommendation.body: Restore writable mount and fs-bridge semantics for the sandbox workspace only, with explicit tests that `/agent`, real workspace paths, and skill roots remain protected.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original read-only behavior and has the strongest visible sandbox/security history in this path.
